title: Coverage-Loss Discount Calculation (Hospital Account (Encounter Billing))
content:
**Clause.** On a Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) account, the coverage-loss amount is the total of the account's coverage-terminated liability postings; an account with none has a coverage-loss amount of 0.00 and receives no coverage-loss discount. The coverage-loss discount percent starts from the patient class's elective uninsured discount percent for an account classified elective non-covered, and from the patient class's uninsured discount percent for any other account (both from the uninsured discount schedule). The coverage-loss discount is that percent of the coverage-loss amount, rounded half-up to the cent.

**Combination.** Percentage points and dollar amounts are combined with that figure this way: every allowance stated in percentage points is added to the coverage-loss discount percent; the combined percent is applied once to the coverage-loss amount and rounded half-up to the cent; every amount stated in dollars is then added to that figure; and the resulting coverage-loss discount never exceeds the coverage-loss amount.

## Starting percent

| Service classification of the account | Starting percent |
|---|---|
| elective non-covered | elective uninsured discount percent of the patient class |
| emergency or medically necessary | uninsured discount percent of the patient class |

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

- Coverage-terminated postings of 1800.00 and 1200.00 give a coverage-loss amount of 3000.00. On a medically necessary account of a patient class whose uninsured discount percent were 45, the coverage-loss discount is 45 percent of 3000.00, that is 1350.00.
- The same account classified elective non-covered, on a class whose elective percent were 20, receives 600.00.
- *Combination (hypothetical).* With 5 percentage points added and a 200.00 dollar amount, 50 percent of 3000.00 is 1500.00 and the discount is 1700.00; had the figures summed past 3000.00, the discount would stop at 3000.00.
